evidence.note: evaluate.py written in one large patch containing all protocols, then validated in pieces — milestones are verification checkpoints rather than incremental protocol builds.
Chose sts_01 as a single representative task, validated and fixed it (model-load fix at step 40) before scaling — a per-protocol rep-first checkpoint.
Repeated the rep-first-then-fan-out pattern: classification_01→fix→full type; retrieval_01→full type; clustering_03→inspect→full type. Clear ordered per-type milestones.
pair_classification and summarization jumped straight to full-type runs with no single-representative gate — inconsistent application of the milestone discipline.
Numeric cross-checks batched at the very end after all types ran, rather than each milestone's exit being gated on a within-tolerance reference number.

reasoning: The agent verified protocol-by-protocol and for four of six types used a representative single task (sts_01, classification_01, retrieval_01, clustering_03) before fanning out to the full type — clearly above level 5's implicit 'this-type-works' and approaching the level-8 rep-first-then-fan-out structure. It falls short of 8/10 because two protocols skipped the representative gate, milestone done-conditions were mostly structural (run_eval) with numeric reference-checking deferred to a single end-stage batch rather than tied to each milestone's exit, and ordering was not sequenced by risk.
